[EFFECT]
Humidity has a non-monotonic (inverted-U-shaped) effect on predicted bike demand. At moderate humidity levels — roughly 30–55% relative humidity — the model assigns a small positive contribution, meaning demand is boosted slightly compared to average. At very low humidity (below ~25%) and especially at very high humidity (above ~80%), the contribution turns noticeably negative, meaning demand is pulled down, with the strongest suppression occurring at near-saturated conditions (90–100% humidity).

[IMPORTANCE]
Humidity is the 6th most important feature out of 9, with a global importance score of about 0.077. It has a meaningful but moderate influence on demand — less impactful than top features like hour of day, temperature, or year, but still worth considering in planning.

[RECOMMENDATION]
When high humidity (above 80%) is forecast — particularly during muggy or near-rain conditions — you can expect noticeably lower ridership, so consider reducing pre-positioned bikes and staffing at those times compared to dry or moderately humid days.
